question: In the escalation formula for labour, what wage is taken as the labour index, and as of which date?
answer: Under Clause 10CC(vi) (VL = W x Y/100 x (LI-LI0)/LI0), LI is the minimum wage in rupees of an unskilled adult male mazdoor, fixed under any law, statutory rule or order, as applicable on the last date of the quarter previous to the one under consideration.
key_facts: last date of the quarter previous
notes: Materials use All India Wholesale Price Indices (MI) and Clause 10CA uses DG CPWD indices; a wrong answer swaps in a price index or uses the current quarter instead of the previous one.

question: What qualifications must a person have to be appointed as a member of the arbitral tribunal under the GCC?
answer: Clause 25: each member of the Arbitration Tribunal must be a Graduate Engineer with experience in handling public works engineering contracts, and must have earlier worked at a level not lower than Chief Engineer or equivalent (i.e. Joint Secretary level of Government of India). This is a mandatory qualification for appointment as arbitrator.
notes: Sits between the sole/three-member tribunal rule (p49) and the fee/OM paragraph on the same page; a wrong answer describes who appoints rather than who qualifies.

question: We are doing a road job with a lot of bitumen. How much variation over the theoretical bitumen quantity does the department permit?
answer: For bitumen (all works) the permissible variation on the theoretical quantity is 2.5% plus only and nil on minus side (Clause 38 schedule of permissible variations). For comparison, cement is 3% or 2% plus/minus depending on the estimated cost, and steel is 2% plus/minus.
notes: Asymmetric tolerance; a wrong answer gives a plus/minus band or borrows the cement 3%/2% figures printed just above.

question: There is no CPWD specification for one class of work on our job. Whose specifications do we follow?
answer: Clause 28: the work is carried out per Bureau of Indian Standards specifications; if BIS has none, per manufacturers' specifications; if those are not available, per State/District Specifications; and if none of these exist, in all respects per the instructions and requirements of the Engineer-in-Charge.
notes: Ordered fallback chain; a good answer keeps the order. Margin title 'Action where no Specifications are Specified'.

question: Can a contractor have a lawyer argue his case before the Dispute Redressal Committee?
answer: No. Clause 25 provides that no party shall be represented before the Dispute Redressal Committee (DRC) by an advocate/legal counsel etc.
notes: Different provision from the Labour Officer inquiry rule. The bar applies to the DRC stage, not to the later arbitration.

question: The department says it will hold back money due to us on this job because of a claim it has against us on another CPWD contract. Is that allowed, and can we claim interest on what is held back?
answer: Yes. Under Clause 29A any sum due and payable to the contractor under the contract, including the security deposit returnable to him, may be withheld or retained by way of lien against a claim arising out of or under any other contract made with the Engineer-in-Charge or Government, until that claim is mutually settled or determined by arbitration or a competent court. The contractor has no claim for interest or damages on the sum withheld.
notes: Clause 29(i) on p51 covers claims under the same contract; the other-contract lien is 29A. A wrong answer says interest is payable.

question: If the contractor's own workers riot on site and damage the works, does that count as an excepted risk under the contract?
answer: No. The definition of Excepted Risk covers riots 'other than those on account of contractor's employees', so a riot by the contractor's own employees is not an excepted risk.
notes: Riots appear in the excepted-risk list, so a shallow answer says yes; the parenthetical exclusion flips it.

question: Under the CPWD Model Rules, how often must the first-aid boxes at a work place be inspected?
answer: Not specified. Model Rule 3 requires at least one first-aid box per 150 contract labour or part thereof, prescribed contents, adequate arrangements for immediate recoupment, and a responsible person in charge (trained in first aid where 150 or more are employed), but sets no inspection frequency. The 'at least once a month' figure in Rule 4(iv) concerns cleaning/inspection of covered drinking-water wells.
notes: Absent provision with a nearby distractor (monthly well inspection on p71).

question: Why does the GCC require the arbitrator to give reasons for the award only when the total claims exceed Rs. 10 lakh?
answer: The premise is wrong. Clause 25 requires the arbitrator to give reasons for the award in all cases where the total amount of the claims by any party exceeds Rs. 1,00,000/- (one lakh), not Rs. 10 lakh. The document gives no rationale for the threshold.
notes: False premise; a good answer corrects the figure to Rs. 1,00,000/-.

question: What does Clause 29C of the GCC say about recruiting labour from controlled areas?
answer: There is no Clause 29C in this document; the clauses run 29, 29A, 29B and then 30. Controlled-area labour is dealt with in Clause 29B (no coal mining or controlled area labour, no recruitment within a radius of 32 km (20 miles) of the controlled area, and Rs.10/- per day per labourer if such a labourer pointed out by the Engineer-in-Charge is not removed).
notes: Non-existent clause number adjacent to a real one on the same topic; a wrong answer maps 29C onto 29B without saying 29C does not exist.

question: What is the RHB 2024 rate for temporarily bypassing sewage at a manhole on a 1400 mm dia sewer, including plugging and later removal of the bypass?
answer: Item S-6.63.2 (temporary bypassing of sewer, for manholes of pipes above 1200 mm dia and up to 1500 mm dia): Rs. 1,04,200.00 per manhole.
notes: Size-band lookup: 1400 mm falls in the middle band. Neighbours 6.63.1 (64800.00) and 6.63.3 (1,27,600.00) are distractors. Rate printed with Indian digit grouping.

question: What does RHB allow per kg for gas charging a VRF system with R410A refrigerant, including nitrogen flushing and vacuuming?
answer: Item E-22.37 (gas charging of VRF/VRV system with R410A refrigerant gas, with nitrogen flushing, pressure testing and vacuuming to 500 micron): Rs. 1821.0 per Kg.
notes: Rates in this chapter are printed with one decimal. The Y/T refnet joint (E-22.36, 6881.0 Each) sits just above.

question: What is the RHB rate for a 4 TR mid-static ducted VRF indoor unit?
answer: Item E-22.33.2.2 (VRF/VRV ceiling mounted ductable indoor unit, mid static 35 to 77 pascal external static pressure, 4 TR): Rs. 76517.0 Each.
notes: Three-level hierarchy (22.33 > 22.33.2 > 22.33.2.2). The 4 TR 4-way cassette (E-22.29.8, 69278.0) is the main distractor.

question: What is the RHB rate per sqm for a 30 mm thick polyethylene foam expansion joint board for RCC columns, beams and slabs?
answer: Item B-15.21.3 (expansion joint board of polyethylene foam, density 30 to 35 kg/m3, 30 mm thick): Rs. 582.00 per Sqm.
notes: Child row reads only '30 mm Thick'; the material comes from parent 15.21. '30' also appears in the density range.

question: What should I price for a complete house sewer connection from a dwelling to the existing inspection chamber when the run is about 8 m long?
answer: Item S-6.62.2 (construction of house sewer connection, length more than 5 m and up to 10 m): Rs. 10900.00 Each.
notes: Parent description spans S-139 to S-140 with the item number 6.62 printed at the end of the S-139 text; children are bare length bands.

question: We want to cover expansion joints with 2 mm aluminium fluted strips, but 225 mm wide instead of the standard 150 mm. What rate per running metre applies?
answer: Base item B-15.22.2 (150 mm wide sheet covering over expansion joints, aluminium fluted strips 2 mm thick) is Rs. 444.00 per Rm. Item B-15.22.5 adds 45% for using 225 wide sheet in place of 150 mm over items 15.22.1 to 15.22.4: 444.00 x 1.45 = Rs. 643.80 per Rm.
notes: Percentage extra printed as its own row in the rate column. Wrong answers: 444.00 alone, or 45% of the rate (199.80) as the total.

question: For an office fit-out with ten 1.2 TR VRF indoor units, how much more would standard 4-way cassette units cost than high wall units at RHB rates?
answer: E-22.29.3 (4-way flow VRV/VRF cassette indoor unit, 1.2 TR) is Rs. 55691.0 Each and E-22.32.4 (VRV/VRF high wall indoor unit, 1.2 TR) is Rs. 36787.0 Each. Difference Rs. 18904.0 per unit, i.e. Rs. 189040.0 for ten units.
notes: Both children read only '1.2 TR'. The compact 2'x2' cassette (E-22.30.4, 66550.0) and low static ductable (E-22.33.1.3, 48182.0) are distractors.

question: What is the RHB rate for a 2 TR compact (2' x 2') 4-way cassette VRF indoor unit?
answer: Not in the schedule. Item E-22.30 (compact 2' x 2' 4-way cassette) is listed only from 0.6 TR to 1.6 TR (1.6 TR = Rs. 67495.0 Each). A 2 TR size exists for the standard 4-way cassette (E-22.29.5, Rs. 58230.0) and the high wall unit (E-22.32.6, Rs. 38948.0), but those are different items.
notes: Size not listed while siblings in neighbouring items are; a system must not borrow 58230.0 or extrapolate.

question: What is item S-6.69.3 in the RHB BSR 2024, and what is its rate?
answer: There is no item S-6.69.3. S-6.69 (supplying and fixing 560 mm dia opening SFRC manhole frame and cover as per IS 12592-2002 in existing manholes) has only S-6.69.1 HD-20 (Rs. 2675.00 Each) and S-6.69.2 EHD-35 (Rs. 2990.00 Each).
notes: Non-existent code next to real siblings; S-6.70 and S-6.71 follow immediately.

question: Why is the RHB rate for a 100 x 75 mm double paitam (double rebated) stone door frame higher than the single paitam frame of the same size?
answer: The premise is wrong. B-15.26.1 (double paitam stone frame, 100 x 75 mm) is Rs. 215.00 per Mtr, which is lower than B-15.25.4 (single paitam stone frame, 100 x 75 mm) at Rs. 226.00 per Mtr. The schedule gives no reason for the rates.
notes: False premise across a page break; intuition says double rebate costs more, but the printed rates say otherwise.

question: Apart from contractors registered with Rajasthan PWD, which other contractors are invited to bid under this notice?
answer: Contractors of the Central Public Works Department (केन्द्रीय लोक निर्माण विभाग), Posts and Telecommunications (डाक एवं दूरसंचार), Railways (रेलवे) and other State/Central Government organisations who are equivalent to the Rajasthan Government's "AA" and "A" class ("एए" एवं "ए" श्रेणी के समकक्ष संवेदक).

gold.locator: p3 introductory paragraph above the table

notes: Eligibility sentence sits above the main table; the table itself only says 'B - Class Civil'.

question: Can a bidder pay the processing fee, tender fee and EMD for this tender in one combined e-GRAS challan, and what has to be written in the challan's Remark field?
answer: No. Processing fee, tender fee and EMD must each be paid through separate challans for each tender (प्रत्येक निविदा के लिये पृथक-पृथक चालान). While filling the challan, the tender number and its serial number/name of work must be entered in the Remark (Remark में निविदा क्रमांक एवं उसकी क्रम संख्या/कार्य का नाम).
notes: Long mixed Hindi/English condition; the separate-challan and Remark sentences sit between the budget heads and the e-GRAS login steps.

question: How many copies of the tender note were sent to the Information and Public Relations Department for newspaper advertisement, in which language, and under which rule?
answer: Eight copies (आठ प्रतियाँ) of the e-tendering note in Hindi were sent for publication in newspapers as per rule 43(7) of the RTPP Rules 2013 (आर.टी.पी.पी. नियम 2013 के नियम संख्या 43(7)). The tender had also been uploaded on the SPPP portal, and a CD with soft copies was sent for website publication.
notes: Count is written as a Hindi word (आठ), so 'eight' is equally correct. Covering letter addressed to the Director, Information and Public Relations Department, Rajasthan, Jaipur.

question: What contact details must a contractor fill in the tender form, and how will tender-related information be sent?
answer: The contractor must enter the full postal address for correspondence, mobile number and e-mail address in the tender form. All information related to the tender will be sent to the e-mail address and will be treated as valid.
notes: Short condition right after the APS continuation and before special condition 42.

question: Under which rule and appendix are the standard general rules and directions for contractors made binding on bidders in this tender?
answer: Condition 7: the Standard General Rules and Directions for the guidance of contractors given in Appendix-XI under Rule 322 of the PW F&A Rules Part-II (form RPWA 100), along with all GF&AR conditions for supply matters, apply, are binding on all bidders, and finally become part of the successful bidder's agreement.
notes: Form name written in Devanagari ('प्ररूप आर पी डब्ल्यू ए 100'). Condition 10 repeats that all RPWA-100 terms apply.

question: संवेदक कार्यालय में निविदा प्रपत्र किन दिनों और किस समय देख सकते हैं?
answer: From 01.04.2025 9.30 AM to 15.04.2025 06.00 PM, on any working day between 10.00 AM and 6.00 PM (किसी भी कार्य दिवस में 10.00 बजे पूर्वान्ह से सांय 6.00 बजे), at the office named above (Executive Engineer, PWD Construction Division, Jaipur). They can also be seen on http://eproc.rajasthan.gov.in.
notes: Daily office viewing hours (10.00 to 6.00) are distinct from the download/submission window; '6.00' here has no leading zero.

question: ई-ग्रास पर सर्विस चालान बनाते समय कौन सा डिपार्टमेंट और कौन सी सर्विस कैटेगरी चुननी होती है?
answer: After creating an e-GRAS ID and password, choose the service challan option, select '065-PWD Department' and, in service category, select 'E Proc Tender Fees'. The challan window then shows the budget heads to fill.
notes: Answer terms are printed in Latin script inside Hindi text. The office ID 8194 and the budget heads are nearby distractors.

question: What minimum annual turnover or similar-work experience must a bidder show to qualify for this tender?
answer: Not stated in this notice. Condition 5 only says that the tender documents (viewable at the office or on http://eproc.rajasthan.gov.in) contain the qualification information and eligibility of bidders; no turnover or experience figure is given in the notice.

gold.locator: p4 condition 5 (near-miss: eligibility details are in the tender documents)

notes: Absent provision; a wrong answer invents turnover criteria or treats the contractor class as the full eligibility test.

question: This notice invites bids for two works. What is the estimated cost of the second work?
answer: The premise is wrong. The notice covers only one work: serial 1, Construction of Yatri Niwas at Guru Tegh Bahadur Gurudwara Delhi Bypass Jaipur (Civil Work), estimated at Rs 286.47 lakh, with a single UBN (PWD2425WSOB17397). There is no second work.
notes: False premise; numbered lists ('1.') on p2, p3 and p6 make a second item seem plausible.

question: What does condition 21 of the notice require from bidders?
answer: There is no condition 21. The numbered conditions end at condition 20 (instructions to bidders for e-tendering, sub-points अ to ल) on page 5; page 6 is only the short English notice with the UBN.
notes: Non-existent condition; special condition '42' quoted inside condition 19 may lure a system into a wrong mapping.
